note: No corpus. The input is the run report `e2e/bench-journey-teacher-loop.spec.ts` writes, and this file is the contract between the two so neither has to guess at the other's shape.

reportShape.completed: 1 when the loop closed — queue, student, a recorded action, back to the queue
reportShape.teacherTaps: controls the instructor pressed, including the two navigations they make themselves; typing is not a tap
reportShape.queueToActionSeconds: from opening the queue to the action being recorded — the half of the loop an instructor feels
reportShape.totalSeconds: wall clock for the whole run
reportShape.stepCount: how many steps the spec walked, checked against expectedStepCount
reportShape.measuredAt: ISO instant, so a stale report can be recognised

ageNote: A report older than this is treated as absent rather than scored. A green `completed: 1` from last week, reported against today's commit, is a passing gate that measured nothing.

designFloors.note: The design proposes 6 taps or fewer (spec section 4.6, marked with a dagger). Not set as a floor yet: no run has established today's number, and the authoring worktree had no dev server or database. Set the baseline from the first CI run, then floor it.

actionNote: The recorded action is a case note rather than the seeded pending orientation verification. Verifying is the better story and consumes the fixture — the second run would find nothing pending and quietly measure a shorter loop. A case note is a real recorded action (POST /api/teacher/students/[id]/notes, audit-logged) that can be taken again tomorrow.
howToRun: npm run dev   # or npm run start against a build
workersNote: --workers=1 is not optional. /api/auth/login rate-limits to 10 attempts per IP per 15 minutes, and parallel specs sharing one IP exhaust it and fail with 429 (see the standing note in .claude/MEMORY.md).
